title: durability-of-stones-is-a-lane-on-the-exit-gate
what: The durability of a stone — committed AND pushed — becomes a lane on the PROVED exit gate, composing repo_truth(), so a stone cannot close over work that exists only on this laptop.
why: A green stone that exists only on this laptop is a green nobody else can lean on, and Law 8 says the whole return on proving is that a peer composes proven code WITHOUT re-checking it. The lived symptom is a builder's and it has already happened once, recorded verbatim in the instrument's own docstring: on 2026-07-26 an `echo "cairn pushed"` welded to && attested a push that never happened, and `git status` clean confirmed the wrong thing. Nothing caught it. Today the only thing standing between a proven stone and a disk failure is that CC remembers step 10 of /sail.
how: Compose, do not build. cairn/tools/orient/orient.py:272 repo_truth() already reads HEAD vs @{u} and porcelain dirt from git plumbing for both repos, and its own docstring records the founding failure verbatim (2026-07-26: an `echo "cairn pushed"` welded to && attested a push that never happened). The gate infrastructure also exists: EXIT_GATE = TransitionGate('exit_gate') with _exit_gate(ticket) running lanes on the forward crossing into PROVED (transitions.py:1034,1342). So the build is a LANE, not a machine. THE SHAPE QUESTION, and it is what makes this a ticket rather than a one-liner: a PROVED crossing is ITSELF a write — it appends history.json and moves the cursor — so the tree is necessarily dirty at the moment of crossing, and /sail commits at step 10, AFTER the step-8 PROVED crossing. A lane demanding a clean tree at PROVED would red every voyage. The order-independent predicate that works either way: refuse on COMMITTED-BUT-UNPUSHED work — ahead_of_upstream > 0 — because that is never the current crossing's own doing. One stone's slack, caught at the next stone's close, and it can never be silently skipped because every stone crosses PROVED. The dirty-tree half is MEASURED AND JOURNALED, not refused, so the number exists before anyone argues about the threshold.
traces_to: Law 4 — the durability-of-stones rule has been prose since 2026-07-15 (skills/commit/intention+why.json calls it a GATE that 'belongs on the emit chokepoint as physics, not on a skill someone fires'), and CLAUDE.md:193 says an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect. Also Law 8: proven-space is what a peer leans on, and a stone that exists only on this laptop is not in proven-space anywhere but here — a disk failure makes the green retroactively hollow.
falsifier: DONE when a forward crossing into PROVED with ahead_of_upstream > 0 on either repo raises from the exit gate and names the repo and the count; when the lane composes repo_truth() by import rather than re-shelling git; when dirty_paths is journaled on every PROVED crossing whether or not it refuses; and when the lane's own ticket crosses PROVED through it. WRONG INTENT if it fires constantly and gets an exemption roster — that is the retro-red shape watchme_spec.py:34 records being paid for twice, and the tell is _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER growing a second tenant. Also WRONG if it makes push a reflex rather than a boundary act: pushing after every stone is correct, pushing mid-thought is not, and if the measured effect is more pushes of broken intermediate states the gate moved the defect rather than closing it.
children: none, because the build is a single lane composing an existing instrument at an existing gate — cairn/tools/orient/orient.py:272 repo_truth() and cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:1342 _exit_gate both exist and are proven. There is no absence large enough to split.

out: A DIRTY-TREE REFUSAL. Hard bound: a PROVED crossing is itself a write — it appends history.json and moves the cursor — so porcelain is necessarily nonzero at the moment of crossing and a refusal on it reds every voyage on its first run. dirty_paths is MEASURED AND JOURNALED, never a verdict. This is the one thing a cheap builder will add without being told not to.

An exemption roster. _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER's own comment says it stays EMPTY, and a second roster for this lane is the retro-red shape watchme_spec.py:34 records being paid for twice. If the lane fires too often the answer is the predicate, not a list of names.
A git hook. Fires where the reasoning is gone and cannot name the ticket.
A beat probe as the primary mechanism. The beat already carries ~78 addresses of tail (live trouble beat-tail-re-walks-corpora-no-sieve-counts) and a report is not a refusal.
Touching /commit's behaviour. The skill stays a light checkpoint; its charter's `distinction` field already settled that these coexist.
Narrowing to one repo. A stone's ticket is in the commons and its code is in cairn; durability is the conjunction.

open_for_akien: One, and it is yours because it is a cost you bear, not a fact anyone can measure: SHOULD THE LANE REFUSE WHEN THE PUSH TARGET IS UNREACHABLE? A network outage would turn into a blocked voyage. My read is refuse anyway — a gate that stands down when the network is bad stands down exactly when the work is least durable, and GitHub here is hosting-only with no CI, so an outage has never blocked anything and the cost is a pause, not a broken build. But it is your laptop and your patience, so if you would rather it degrade to a loud journaled warning on an unreachable remote, say so and that is what it does. Everything else on this ticket is settled by measurement or by an existing charter.
